ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: streaming-cont-batch p99 latency breach in us-west-2. current p99=1.9s (SLO=1.2s). paging on-call. :rotating_light:
Maya (on-call): saw the page, jumping in. which services are impacted? any customer-facing errors?
Diego: looks like streaming path only (continuous batching). metrics show CPU/GPU utilization steady, but batch sizes spiked to 64 for short bursts, and tail latency climbed.
Priya: confirming customer impact — a handful of active sessions reported audio-to-text stalls, we have 4 customer sessions with >10s stalls in the logs. no 5xxs.
Maya (on-call): ok — customer-impact = partial degradation for streaming apps. escalate to severity 2. I'll page infra if we need immediate capacity changes.
Elliot: threading note — scheduler log shows many mixed-seq requests (avg seq len 28, but a subset with seq len 720) which forces big batches and KV cache pressure. scheduling fairness counters have high variance.
Claire: ops-bot posted trace sample: https://redwood/trace/abcd. looking at traces, long tail sits inside cont-batch queue wait time.
Maya (on-call): quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch_size on cont-batcher from 64->32 2) enable preemptive-smallreq-priority for 30m 3) add temporary packing-disable flag for stream routes. anyone object?
Diego: good plan. lowering max batch will reduce throughput efficiency but should cut tail. push the config to canary pool first.
Priya: I'll notify customer success / impacted customers if we need >30m mitigation.
Elliot: command to apply canary (on runtime):
```
curl -X POST https://runtime.api/configs/apply 
  -d '{"service":"cont-batcher","env":"us-west-2","changes":{"max_batch_size":32,"scheduling_policy":"preempt-small"}}'
```
Maya (on-call): Diego can you roll that to canary now? tag me in deploy notes.
Diego: rolling canary to batcher-usw2-canary (job id 77321). watching p95/p99.
ops-bot: DEPLOY STARTED: job=77321 user=Diego target=batcher-usw2-canary
Diego: canary up. preliminary numbers: p95 down 15%, p99 down 35% after 5 minutes. queue wait time dropped ~40%.
Claire: good delta. streaming stalls reduced in sample traces. still seeing a small group with >5s due to very long seqs.
Maya (on-call): follow-up: schedule fairness tweak — reduce packing window from 20ms->10ms to avoid mixing tiny + huge seqs. Diego/Elliot, can you test that in canary?
Elliot: will test now. I'll run load test with mixed seq distribution (90% short <64, 10% long >512).
Priya: CS notified affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA 30m.
Diego: packing-window change pushed to canary (job 77322). results: further 10% p99 improvement, and long-seq stall counts cut by ~60% in canary traces.
Maya (on-call): looks promising. plan to roll to production in 10m if no regressions. keep monitoring for KV cache evictions — if evictions spike, we may need to reduce long-seq concurrency instead.
ops-bot: METRICS UPDATE: p95=0.9s p99=1.15s (post-canary), kv-evictions=+8%
Elliot: kv-evictions small but within acceptable delta. rolling to prod now with staggered 5% steps.
Diego: prod roll step 1/20 applied.
Priya: CS updated customers that mitigation complete and we are monitoring.
Maya (on-call): holding for 20m to confirm stability. if p99 stays <=1.2s we close. any outstanding action items?
Claire: follow-up ticket to add automatic preemptive policy when mixed-seq variance > X. I'll create the ticket.
Diego: add runbook note: when streaming p99 >1.5s check mixed-seq ratio and consider immediate max_batch_size reduction.
Maya (on-call): thanks team. closing page if stable at last check. ops-bot, please mark incident as acknowledged and attach links to deploys and traces.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: acknowledged by Maya (on-call). links: deploys 77321,77322 trace samples /trace/abcd,/trace/ef12. severity downgraded to s3.
Maya (on-call): closing thread — will follow up with postmortem draft if any regression in next 24h. :white_check_mark:
